epic.intent:
## Outcome

Turn execution mistakes into durable, reviewable prevention instead of losing them in attempt history. Rejection reasons remain tied to the exact ticket and attempt and are injected into the next retry packet automatically. Every successfully completed sprint produces exactly one idempotent learning Kanban card after checkpoint advance. The same orchestrator claims and delegates that queued card before polling ordinary work in the next sprint, without blocking sprint advancement.

The card receives an immutable evidence snapshot containing rejected attempts, failed or reconciled attempts, failed row and acceptance checks, and the sprint retro's `wentPoorly` and `actions`. Its worker must disposition every item as a reusable learning, a duplicate, or sprint-specific noise; deduplicate the reusable items; propose scoped learning records for workers and/or orchestrators; and add repository guardrails such as tests, lint rules, documentation or skills when those are the stronger prevention.

Repository edits run on isolated learning branches/worktrees rooted at the completed sprint increment. A multi-repository sprint may produce one guarded branch per affected repository under the same card. The card reaches Ready for review without blocking the next sprint. Human approval preflights and integrates every branch, then publishes the learning records; a conflict, failed integration, or kick-back publishes nothing. Published records are selected by role and path into future worker packets and orchestrator context. A Learnings surface shows provenance and applicability and lets a person retire or replace stale guidance.

## Confirmed decisions

- Evidence sources: rejections, failures/reconciliations, failed row and acceptance checks, and retro `wentPoorly`/`actions`.
- Codification may create first-class learning records and any justified repository guardrails.
- Generation happens only after the sprint checkpoint advances; it is non-blocking.
- The same orchestrator picks up the generated card.
- Learning records activate only on human approval.
- Guardrail work is isolated from ongoing sprint work.
- One card may span every affected repository in a repository-folder project.
- People can inspect, retire and replace published learnings.

## Non-goals

- No automatic approval or checkpoint authority for agents.
- No learning becomes active while its card is merely In progress or Ready for review.
- No mutation of historical attempts, reports or retros to retrofit conclusions.
- No checkpoint gate: the next sprint may proceed while codification is being reviewed.
- No blanket conversion of every failure into permanent guidance; the card must justify or dismiss each source item.
- No direct edits to built-in Dark Mechanicus facts in another installation; repository guardrails stay in the project repositories the sprint affected.

## Standards

Each work ticket lists and runs its targeted tests. The sprint acceptance node runs the project's Definition of Done once on the combined increment. No additional tests-first or Fireguard requirement is added by this plan.

successCriteria.text: A rejected ticket's retry packet identifies every earlier rejected attempt with its actionable reasons, review notes and provenance, so a replacement worker does not rely on the orchestrator manually copying the WHY.

After each successful sprint checkpoint advance, exactly one queued learning card is linked to that run and sprint, contains a complete immutable snapshot of all configured learning sources, and is surfaced for the same orchestrator to claim before ordinary next-sprint polling without blocking the run.

A learning-card worker can disposition every source item, submit deduplicated role/path-scoped learning records, and produce isolated guardrail commits rooted at the completed sprint increment for one or several affected repositories; ordinary Kanban cards keep their current behavior.

Approving a learning card recoverably integrates every declared guardrail branch and publishes its learning records only after all integrations pass; conflict, crash recovery and kick-back paths never leave active records claiming guardrails that were not integrated.

Future worker packets and orchestrator context contain only applicable active learning records with evidence provenance, while bounded selection prevents the guidance from overwhelming the execution packet.

A person can inspect each learning's source sprint, tickets, attempts and checks, see its roles and paths, and retire or replace it; portable export/import preserves cards, records, lifecycle state and integration recovery across repository and database storage modes.

epic.title: Sprint learnings: rejection-aware retries and post-sprint codification into durable guardrails

bundle.rationale:
## Evidence inspected

- `rejectAttempt` already persists actionable `reasons` and `notes` on an attempt (`src/core/services/attempts.ts`), but `executionPacket` carries only the current ticket and accepted predecessors; the next worker does not receive earlier rejection decisions.
- The shipped `orchestrator.retry-escalation` fact tells the orchestrator to copy reasons manually, confirming the handoff is procedural rather than enforced.
- Sprint retros already record `wentPoorly` and `actions`, and reports/search preserve them, but no first-class learning lifecycle exists.
- Kanban already supports authorized launch/claim and human-only approval, but ordinary cards work directly on the checked-out branch.
- Knowledge facts already support role/event/topic/path selection and token budgets, but pushed context is orchestrator-only and facts are unmanaged Markdown files.
- The completed SPACE scorecards epic established corrective retrospectives; this epic extends that loop rather than replacing it.

## Selected design

Use immutable evidence plus human-reviewed publication. Rejections reach retries immediately as exact attempt history. A successful checkpoint advance atomically creates and queues one special learning card from a deterministic evidence snapshot. The same orchestrator claims it as its next procedural action, but the run and next sprint remain unblocked. The worker classifies every source item and may propose both scoped learning records and concrete repository guardrails. Guardrail work uses branches/worktrees rooted at the completed increment. Human approval prepares and recoverably integrates all repositories before one final transaction publishes records and completes the card. Active records reuse bounded role/path/event selection for future worker packets and orchestrator context. Humans can later retire or replace records without deleting history.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Prompt-only copying of rejection reasons:** cheap, but it is the current failure mode and remains dependent on orchestrator memory.
- **Publish a fact immediately on every rejection:** fast, but turns one reviewer's local observation into unreviewed permanent authority and amplifies noise.
- **Make codification a next-sprint plan ticket or checkpoint gate:** would guarantee ordering, but the person explicitly chose post-completion, non-blocking Kanban work.
- **Use ordinary Kanban direct-checkout edits:** conflicts with the next sprint and violates the selected isolation requirement.
- **Activate records at Ready for review:** lets unreviewed or malicious guidance affect agents before the person approves it.
- **One card per repository:** simplifies Git integration but fragments the requested single sprint-wide synthesis and can publish inconsistent subsets.

## Dependency graph and critical path

The shared contract is first. Lifecycle services and the evidence collector then proceed in parallel. The service unlocks portable records and context delivery; service plus evidence unlock generated-card creation. Card generation unlocks structured isolated submission. Submission then splits into the Git integration engine and core approval state machine; the desktop coordinator joins them. Kanban review UI and Learnings management UI proceed once their underlying APIs exist. Guidance follows stable command/workflow behavior. The end-to-end ticket joins persistence, delivery, approval, both UIs and guidance before the acceptance node. Critical path: contract → service/evidence → generation → submission → Git/core approval → desktop approval → guidance → end-to-end → acceptance.

## Risks and mitigations

- **The next sprint can start before the card is approved.** This is confirmed behavior, not a hidden guarantee. Same-ticket retries still receive raw rejection WHY immediately; cross-ticket codified guidance activates only after approval.
- **Cross-repository Git is not atomic.** Prepare every result before moving targets, persist expected old/new heads, use compare-and-swap updates, record each applied repository, recover from actual Git truth, and publish records only after all heads verify.
- **Self-reinforcing bad guidance or prompt injection.** Evidence and worker output remain task data; schemas contain no capability/approval fields; human approval is mandatory; applicability is bounded; management can retire/replace.
- **Context overload.** Deduplicate, scope by role/path/event, impose a separate budget, and expose omissions.
- **Stale guidance.** Preserve provenance and replacement chains and provide human retirement/replacement controls.
- **Legacy/storage drift.** Version strict portable records, migrate forward only, keep optional fields absent on older records, and test repo/database round trips.

## Verification strategy

Each work ticket runs only its targeted tests and typecheck when it changes types. The dedicated lifecycle ticket proves assembled single- and multi-repository behavior and captures real Electron evidence. The sprint acceptance node runs the project's Definition of Done exactly once on the combined increment and checks every ticket through a covering criterion. No additional tests-first or Fireguard requirement is imposed by this plan.

## Required-leftover recovery proposal
DM-721 failed its first bounded attempt; management and approved-publication/provenance are split without deleting original scope. The sanctioned retro redraft moves it and its dependents to Sprint 2. DM-720/DM-724 remain accepted in Sprint 1. This is a proposed recovery checkpoint, not a delivered user feature. It adds one full acceptance/report/human checkpoint cost. The active Sprint 1 goal and exit criteria are intentionally NOT rewritten by this agent: they still require the full loop, so the person must explicitly decide/reconcile that recovery boundary in the desktop before adoption/advance. Save alone does not satisfy those unmet outcomes. All complete-loop, Git recovery, UI screenshot and DoD requirements remain in Sprint 2. No additional tests-first or Fireguard requirement is added.

After human review, Save and adoption of the leftover redraft, verify only the accepted foundation and evidence collector remaining in Sprint 1. Run every project Definition of Done command once on the combined integration branch; do not claim the complete learning loop or UI exists.

tickets.title: Sprint 1 acceptance

acceptanceCriteria.text: The shared contract represents a learning's rule, prevention check, roles/events/paths, source run/sprint/card and source evidence ids, active/retired lifecycle, and replacement link without free-form unvalidated authority fields.
The migration upgrades existing databases without altering prior Kanban or run content and enforces one generated learning card per run and sprint.
Malformed or oversized learning records and invalid lifecycle links are rejected by focused tests.

tickets.body:
## Context
Introduce the first-class record that approval publishes. It must carry the prevention rule, applicability, immutable evidence provenance, lifecycle state, replacement links and the source learning card. The database also needs a unique run/sprint → generated-card link and durable integration state. Preserve older databases and imported records.

## In scope
- Strict shared types and validation limits for learning drafts, active/retired records, evidence references, role/event/path applicability and replacement/supersession.
- SQLite migration and indexes for learning records, generated sprint-card identity and integration recovery metadata.
- Compatibility defaults that do not change hashes of older Kanban/run records.

## Out of scope
Commands, packet selection, portable import/export and UI.

## Source locations
- `src/shared/domain/learnings.ts` (new): follow the strict domain vocabulary beside `src/shared/domain/knowledge.ts` and `src/shared/domain/kanban.ts`.
- `src/core/db/migrations.ts`: add the next forward-only schema migration and indexes.
- `src/core/db/migrations.test.ts`: extend clean-install and upgrade coverage.

## Tests
- Add focused schema tests for invalid roles/events, unsafe paths, missing provenance, replacement cycles/self-links and size limits.
- Extend migration tests for upgrade preservation, uniqueness and clean-install parity.
- Run `npx vitest run src/core/db/migrations.test.ts src/shared/domain/learnings.test.ts` and `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: Persistent lifecycle and recovery invariants are hard to repair after records ship.

tickets.title: Define versioned learning records and storage invariants

acceptanceCriteria.text: List/get commands expose stored guidance and provenance to readers while agent roles cannot retire, replace or publish records; malformed management inputs fail schema checks.

Human retire and content-based replacement require an explicit reason and matching revision; replacement creates a linked new version, retires its predecessor, preserves original evidence, and rejects stale concurrent edits.
Management changes preserve append-only searchable history with source links, and focused service/command/schema/migration tests plus typecheck and changed-file lint pass.

tickets.body:
## Recovery context
DM-721 attempt 1 stopped incomplete within its ten-minute window. Its isolated partial commit 3e2bf69b1bb893827cdbde96f4518b4aa7132f04 (work/learnings-DM721) is reference material, not accepted or integration-ready. Do not merge it wholesale: it also contains incomplete publication code assigned to the next ticket. Extract only this ticket's necessary changes into a new worktree from the named sprint integration base.

## Outcome and boundaries
Finish the read and human management half of the original DM-721 contract. Provide list/get, retirement with an explicit reason, and content-based replacement that creates a linked new record/version while retiring the predecessor. Preserve the original immutable evidence provenance and searchable history. Use optimistic revision checks; stale concurrent edits fail explicitly. Agent roles may read but cannot retire, replace or publish guidance. This ticket owns shared management types, command/capability wiring, revision storage and indexed management events. It does not implement staging/publication, portable export, selection, card generation, Git integration or UI.

## Source locations
- `src/core/services/learnings.ts` and `src/core/services/learnings.test.ts`: verified partial load/list/retire/replace functions; replace the prepublished-replacementId approach with replacement content and required reason. Keep management tests separate from publication tests.
- `src/core/commands/learnings.ts`, `src/core/commands/index.ts`, `src/core/commandSchemas.ts`, `src/core/commands/capabilities.ts`, `src/core/authz.ts`, `src/shared/domain/api.ts`, `src/test/stubApi.ts`: verified partial read and desktop-only management wiring; keep only the commands this ticket implements.
- `src/core/db/migrations.ts`: partial additive v23 revision/index support; preserve forward-only migration and existing rows, without adopting unfinished publication staging tables unless required by the following ticket.
- `src/shared/domain/learnings.ts`: accepted bounded content/lifecycle/provenance validators; preserve source identity and replacement invariants.

## Tests
Extend management tests for read authorization, human-only mutations, required reason, new-version replacement, immutable provenance/history, retirement exclusion, stale revisions and search. Extend command capability/schema tests for each implemented command and migration upgrade tests if storage changes. Run the management test file, src/core/commands/capabilities.test.ts, src/core/schemas.test.ts, affected migration tests, changed-file lint and npm run typecheck. Leave full Definition of Done to sprint acceptance. One worker, no nested delegation; five-minute evidence checkpoint and ten-minute stop apply.

reasoning.rationale: Publication is an authority boundary: agents may propose guidance but only human actions activate or retire it.

tickets.title: Complete human learning management and searchable history

acceptanceCriteria.text: Export and import round-trip active, retired and replaced learnings and their immutable provenance without changing semantic hashes.
An interrupted integration manifest is recoverable after restart or clone/import and never implies that its learning is already active.
Malformed, linked, escaping or conflicting learning records are rejected independently and surfaced in reconcile results; database mode settles the same outbox entries without files.

tickets.body:
## Context
Learning records and pending multi-repository integrations must survive restart, clone/import and repository/database storage modes with the same safety rules as plans and Kanban records.

## In scope
- Owned paths and strict portable record schemas for learning definitions, lifecycle events and integration recovery manifests.
- Outbox/finalizer/export/import/reconcile behavior, hash checks, path/link containment and conflict reporting.
- Database-only settlement without writing portable files.

## Out of scope
Knowledge selection and UI.

## Tests

- Add traversal, symlink, malformed/hash-conflict and partial-import tests.

tickets.title: Persist learning records and recovery state across storage modes

acceptanceCriteria.text: A second claim after rejection carries all earlier actionable reasons and review notes with stable attempt provenance without manual orchestration text.
Worker packets and orchestrator context include only active role/path/event matches, report what the budget omitted, and exclude retired or superseded records.
Legacy first claims and ordinary knowledge facts retain their existing shape and precedence, and learning text grants no capability or authority.

tickets.body:
## Context
Today `rejectAttempt` stores reasons on the attempt, but `executionPacket` omits prior attempts; the retry depends on the orchestrator copying text manually. Fix that contract and reuse bounded knowledge selection for approved learning records.

## In scope
- Add prior rejected/failed attempt context to retry packets with attempt number/id, reasons, review notes and timestamps; preserve exact reviewer text.
- Select active learnings for the worker role using ticket file references and a dedicated token budget, with explicit omitted metadata.
- Convert active orchestrator learnings into the existing event/path selection pipeline without allowing them to override authorization or built-in always-apply rules.
- Keep first attempts and legacy records compatible.

## Source locations
- `src/core/services/attempts.ts`: `executionPacket`, `rejectAttempt` and claim tests.
- `src/shared/domain/views.ts`: extend `ExecutionPacket`.
- `src/core/knowledge/select.ts` and `src/core/knowledge/push.ts`: merge approved record candidates into bounded selection.
- `src/core/services/attempts.review.test.ts`, `src/core/knowledge/select.test.ts`, `src/core/commands/knowledgePush.test.ts`: regression coverage.

## Tests
- Add a reject-then-reclaim test proving exact reasons/notes/provenance reach attempt 2 and do not appear on attempt 1.
- Add worker and orchestrator scope/path/budget tests, including omitted records and retired/replaced records.
- Run the targeted attempt and knowledge tests plus `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: The packet must combine historical review evidence with bounded scoped guidance without breaking legacy claims.

tickets.title: Deliver rejection WHY and applicable learnings in execution context

acceptanceCriteria.text: The snapshot contains every configured source kind with stable run/sprint/ticket/attempt/check/report provenance and no reporter-invented facts.
Repeated collection of unchanged state is byte-stable, while the latest report revision and standing row/check outcomes are represented correctly.
A sprint with no negative evidence still produces a valid empty snapshot so downstream generation remains one-card-per-sprint.

tickets.body:
## Context
The generated card needs complete facts, not a reporter's paraphrase. Build one deterministic collector over the pinned run revision and latest accepted sprint report.

## In scope
- Collect rejected attempt reasons/notes, failed and reconciled attempts, latest failed row checks, failed/skipped acceptance checks, and retro `wentPoorly`/`actions`.
- Attach stable source ids, display keys, repository/path references where known, timestamps and normalized fingerprints for deduplication.
- Preserve every source item; classification happens later on the card.

## Out of scope
Creating cards or deciding what becomes a permanent rule.

## Source locations
- `src/core/services/learningEvidence.ts` (new): follow read-model patterns in `src/core/services/reports.ts` and `src/core/services/execution.ts`.
- `src/shared/domain/learnings.ts`: snapshot types from the contract ticket.
- `src/core/services/reports.ts`, `src/core/services/checkpoints.ts`: read-only integration points only where necessary.

## Tests
- Add deterministic fixtures covering every source kind, repeated report revisions, superseded attempts, accepted reruns after a failed row check, legacy null retros and no-learning sprints.
- Prove stable ordering and fingerprints across repeated collection.
- Run `npx vitest run src/core/services/learningEvidence.test.ts` and `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: The collector joins several execution sources and must distinguish historical failures from current standing outcomes.

tickets.title: Build an immutable sprint learning evidence snapshot

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every successful sprint advance creates and queues exactly one linked learning card after the checkpoint is recorded, including the final sprint and an empty evidence snapshot.
Replays and alternate advance paths return the same card and never duplicate card, Play or event records; a failed advance creates nothing.
The advanced run exposes the pending learning card to the owning orchestrator while next-sprint readiness remains non-blocking.

tickets.body:
## Context
Create the post-sprint work only after the checkpoint transition succeeds. It must be idempotent for explicit `advance_sprint`, desktop `approve_and_advance`, auto continuation and replay. It is non-blocking but is the orchestrator's next procedural priority.

## In scope
- Add a special sprint-learning Kanban card kind linked to epic/run/sprint/report/revision and the immutable evidence snapshot.
- Inside successful advancement, create exactly one card, mark its Play pending, and record completed increment bases for every affected repository.
- Expose the queued card id/state in the advance/run read model and `checkpoint.approved` context so the same orchestrator claims it before normal next-sprint polling.
- Generate a card even for an empty snapshot; its worker may conclude there is no reusable rule.

## Out of scope
Claim packet details, submission and approval integration.

## Source locations
- `src/core/services/checkpoints.ts`: `advance`, `moveToSprint`, `completeRun`.
- `src/core/services/kanban/cards.ts`: internal generated-card insertion beside `insertCard`.
- `src/shared/domain/kanban.ts` and `src/shared/domain/views.ts`: card kind/source and run linkage views.
- `src/core/commands/checkpoints.ts`: pushed context/read-model return.

## Tests
- Extend checkpoint control tests for intermediate/final sprint, explicit/desktop/auto paths, replay and transaction rollback.
- Add generation tests proving one queued card, exact snapshot and repository bases, with no checkpoint gate.
- Run targeted checkpoint/Kanban generation tests and `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: Checkpoint completion, idempotency and generated work must commit atomically across every advancement path.

tickets.title: Generate and queue one learning card after checkpoint advance

acceptanceCriteria.text: A learning-card packet names an isolated branch rooted at the completed sprint increment for every affected repository and carries the immutable evidence snapshot; an ordinary card packet is unchanged.
Submission is refused unless every source item has exactly one justified disposition and every proposed learning has bounded role/path applicability and evidence provenance.
Every guardrail manifest is read-only verified against its recorded repository, base, branch and commit before the card reaches Ready for review.

tickets.body:
## Context
A generated card differs from an ordinary card: it starts from completed sprint increments, may span repositories, must disposition every evidence item, and submits proposed records plus guardrail commit manifests. Preserve ordinary card behavior byte-for-byte.

## In scope
- Learning packet fields: immutable snapshot, one base/branch/worktree instruction per affected repository, and reporting contract.
- Deterministic safe branch names and replay-safe claims using the existing secret/lease behavior.
- Submission schema for evidence dispositions (`learning`, `duplicate`, `not_reusable` with reason), proposed learning drafts, and per-repository base/branch/commit manifests.
- Read-only Git verification that every named commit exists, descends from its recorded sprint base, and matches the submitted branch; no merge occurs here.

## Source locations
- `src/core/services/kanban/attempts.ts`: `packetOf`, `claimKanbanCard`, `submitKanbanCard`.
- `src/core/services/learningBranches.ts` (new): branch plan and verification, following `src/core/services/incrementVerify.ts`.
- `src/shared/domain/kanban.ts`, `src/core/commandSchemas.ts`: discriminated packet/submission contracts.

## Tests
- Add single/multi-repository packet tests, claim replay/lost-token behavior, complete disposition coverage and ordinary-card compatibility.
- Add Git fixtures for wrong base, missing branch/commit, unrelated commit and valid manifests.
- Run targeted Kanban attempt/branch verification tests and `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: A special card spans untrusted evidence, secret claims and multiple Git repositories while preserving ordinary-card compatibility.

tickets.title: Claim learning cards with isolated branches and structured codification output

acceptanceCriteria.text: All repository results are prepared and conflict-checked before any target branch moves, under deterministic operation locks.
Each target update is compare-and-swap guarded and a crash after a partial multi-repository apply resumes from actual Git truth without rewriting completed repositories.
A conflict or concurrent target movement leaves the card Ready for review, preserves isolated branches, publishes no guidance and reports the exact repository/action needed.

tickets.body:
## Context
Approval must integrate isolated guardrail branches even if the next sprint has advanced the target branch. Across several repositories there is no single Git transaction, so prepare all results first, persist a manifest, then apply with compare-and-swap and resumable truth. Never move a checked-out branch behind its worktree.

## In scope
- Main-process Git engine that locks each repository in deterministic order, validates clean/owned worktrees and prepares merge or cherry-pick results in temporary worktrees without moving targets.
- Preflight every repository before the first target update; persist planned old/new heads and operation results.
- Apply targets with expected-old-head checks, record each completed update, and recover after crash by reading actual refs/commits.
- Surface conflicts as reviewable failure without publishing learning records or discarding worker branches.

## Out of scope
Core card approval and desktop UI.

## Source locations
- `src/main/git/learningIntegration.ts` (new): follow safe argument, operation-lock and conflict patterns in `src/main/git/branches.ts`, `src/main/git/operationLock.ts`, and `src/main/git/conflicts.ts`.
- `src/shared/git/learningIntegration.ts` (new): manifest/result contracts.
- `src/main/git/learningIntegration.test.ts`: real temporary single/multi-repository fixtures.

## Tests
- Test clean fast path, non-fast-forward preparation, merge conflict before updates, concurrent head movement, crash after one repository update, idempotent resume and checked-out worktree safety.
- Run `npx vitest run src/main/git/learningIntegration.test.ts` and `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: Cross-repository Git updates cannot be atomic and need explicit crash recovery and worktree safety.

tickets.title: Prepare recoverable guardrail integrations across repositories

acceptanceCriteria.text: Preparation binds one submitted attempt, its proposed records and exact repository manifests to a durable operation; later card changes make it stale rather than silently rebinding.
Finalization approves the card and publishes all records in one transaction only after every repository receipt and current head verifies.
Conflict, crash, kick-back and idempotent replay paths preserve recoverable state and never affect ordinary Kanban approval semantics.

tickets.body:
## Context
Core must bind the exact Ready-for-review attempt, proposed records and verified branch manifests to one integration operation. Publication happens only after Git proves every prepared result landed. Kick-back and ordinary-card approval retain their current behavior.

## In scope
- Human-only prepare/read/finalize commands or internal service steps with idempotency and stale-submission guards.
- Persist the integration manifest before Git work, accept per-repository completion receipts, verify actual heads read-only, then publish learning records and mark the card Done in one final transaction.
- Resume/abort semantics for crash, conflict and kick-back; no active records before finalization.

## Source locations
- `src/core/services/kanban/learningApproval.ts` (new): state machine beside `src/core/services/kanban/attempts.ts`.
- `src/core/services/kanban/attempts.ts`: delegate special approval, leave ordinary path unchanged.
- `src/core/commands/kanban.ts`, `src/core/commandSchemas.ts`, `src/shared/domain/api.ts`: desktop integration contract.

## Tests
- Add transition-table tests for prepare, stale attempt, duplicate calls, partial receipts, head mismatch, finalize, kick-back and ordinary-card regression.
- Prove no active records exist before successful finalization.
- Run targeted learning approval and Kanban attempt tests plus `npm run typecheck`.

reasoning.rationale: The state machine joins human authority, Git receipts and database publication without a distributed transaction.

tickets.title: Make learning-card approval a prepare-integrate-publish state machine

acceptanceCriteria.text: One human approval action drives prepare, all repository integrations and final publication, and returns the final Done card only after every step succeeds.
Closing or restarting after partial integration resumes from the durable manifest and actual Git heads; it neither starts a second operation nor republishes records.
Conflicts remain visible on the Ready-for-review card with isolated branches intact, and ordinary card approval still uses its existing path.

tickets.body:
## Context
Only the desktop/person can approve. Route learning cards through the core prepare step, the main-process Git integration engine and core finalization; ordinary cards keep the direct command path. A close or restart during integration must resume visibly.

## In scope
- Main-process coordinator for prepare → Git prepare/apply → receipt recording → finalize, with recovery on desktop start/open.
- Narrow IPC/desktop API used only by the learning-card review action.
- Clear conflict/recovery result returned to the renderer; no hidden retry loops.

## Source locations
- `src/main/kanban/approveLearningCard.ts` (new): follow orchestration/error patterns in `src/main/kanban/startKanbanCard.ts`.
- `src/main/agents/chatHandlers.ts` or the appropriate desktop handler registration, `src/main/desktop/ipc.ts`, `src/preload/index.ts`, `src/shared/desktop/api.ts`: narrow bridge.
- `src/main/kanban/approveLearningCard.test.ts`: injected core/Git fakes plus restart recovery.

## Recovery context
Complete the approved-publication and provenance half extracted from the original DM-721. Partial commit 3e2bf69b1bb893827cdbde96f4518b4aa7132f04 on work/learnings-DM721 contains unaccepted staging/publication sketches; inspect them as reference only. Build from accepted management and collector results, not from the whole failed branch.

## Outcome and boundaries
Provide internal staged-draft and approved-attempt publication functions for the later Kanban workflow. Agents may propose but cannot publish active authority. Bind publication to the exact accepted card attempt; the later prepare/integrate/publish state machine supplies its approved transaction after Git verification. Idempotent replay must never duplicate records or lifecycle events. An empty draft list is a valid no-learning result. Validate every immutable evidence reference against the source run AND sprint/card, source kind, ownership and exact canonical hash. Preserve original evidence text; evidence and proposed learning content grant no authority. Do not add an agent-facing publication command, implement Git/card-approval state machine, portable storage or UI.

## Source locations
- `src/core/services/learnings.ts` (verified partial stageLearningDrafts/publishApprovedLearningDrafts) or new `src/core/services/learningPublication.ts` beside it: isolate publication from accepted management APIs.
- New `src/core/services/learningPublication.test.ts`: follow verified management tests and `src/core/services/learningEvidence.test.ts` fixtures, exercising actual service transitions rather than source text.
- `src/shared/domain/learnings.ts` and `src/shared/domain/learningEvidence.ts`: align strict learning source references with the accepted immutable snapshot sourceId/sourcePath/contentHash contract; do not invent incompatible hash projections.
- `src/core/db/migrations.ts`: add forward-only durable staging/publication identity tables and tests as needed. Partial v23 is unaccepted reference; do not rewrite an accepted migration.
- `src/core/services/kanban/cards.ts`, `src/core/services/execution.ts`, `src/core/services/events.ts`: existing persisted card/attempt/source and append-only event patterns.

## Tests
Add consumer-visible tests for valid approved publication, same-attempt replay without duplicate records/events, unapproved/stale/wrong-card and agent rejection, empty drafts, altered/missing hashes, cross-run/cross-sprint attempts, row/report references, comment/attachment ownership and immutable published provenance. Assert searchable publication history. Run npx vitest run src/core/services/learningPublication.test.ts plus affected learning/migration tests, changed-file lint and npm run typecheck. Full Definition of Done stays at sprint acceptance. Keep one worker within the five/ten-minute evidence window.
